answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by paying only for verified useful work, with rewards that vest slowly, like a glacier releasing meltwater. Each agent's earnings sit in a jade-marked escrow and thaw only as peers attest its outputs over weeks, so a fake identity must do real, costly work for a long time before it can cash out. A single sonnet of praise from a friend unlocks nothing; only a sustained record of attested work does. Attackers face months of compute per identity, while honest agents earn steadily, making thousands of fake agents unprofitable.
